course.title: Flask Web Applications — Local Lab Course
course.subtitle: 17 modules, 84 steps. Reverse-engineered from the LabEx Flask path into a self-contained Docker lab.
course.attribution: Curriculum distilled from LabEx Flask labs, whose code follows the official Flask tutorial (pallets/flask, BSD-3-Clause). See LICENSE-notes.md.

modules.title: Getting Started with the Flask Web Framework
modules.summary: Install Flask, write a route, serve a Jinja template, render dynamic URL values.

modules.title: Flask + Jinja2 Templates
modules.summary: Separate presentation from logic: render_template with a templates/ folder.

modules.title: Working with the Development Server
modules.summary: flask run, --debug reloader and interactive debugger, --app, port conflicts, app.run().

modules.title: The Flask Command Line Interface
modules.summary: flask run, click commands, app.cli.add_command, custom management commands.

modules.title: Building a Flask Application (Application Factory)
modules.summary: Package layout, create_app(), config mapping, instance path, first route.

modules.title: SQLite Database Setup
modules.summary: sqlite3 + g, schema.sql, init_db, CLI command registration, real database file.

modules.title: Modular Application with Blueprints and Authentication
modules.summary: auth blueprint, register/login/logout views, password hashing, session, login_required.

modules.title: Styling the Application with Static Files
modules.summary: static/style.css, url_for('static'), template inheritance, served CSS.

modules.title: The Blog Application (CRUD)
modules.summary: blog blueprint, index JOIN, create/update/delete with author checks.

modules.title: Configuration Management
modules.summary: dict config, from_object, from_pyfile, env-selected config, instance folder.

modules.title: Signals and Application Lifecycle
modules.summary: blinker Namespace, named signals, subscribers, send() during app lifecycle.

modules.title: Working with the Shell and Request Context
modules.summary: flask shell, test_request_context, preprocess_request/process_response, shelltools helpers.

modules.title: Testing Flask Applications (pytest basics)
modules.summary: app/client/runner fixtures, view tests, CLI runner tests.

modules.title: Unit Testing flaskr with pytest and Coverage
modules.summary: conftest fixtures with a temp DB, factory/db/auth/blog suites, coverage report.

modules.title: Secure Web Application Development
modules.summary: XSS escaping, CSRF tokens, JSON security, security headers, cookie flags, HPKP.

modules.title: Async and Await in Flask
modules.summary: async def views, awaited I/O, jsonify payloads.

modules.title: Deploying the Application
modules.summary: build a wheel, install it, instance SECRET_KEY, run under Waitress.

steps.goal: Install Flask and create the app module that the rest of the module builds on.

checks.hint: pip install flask
app.py must import Flask and create an instance: app = Flask(__name__)

steps.goal: Add the first route so the app answers '/' with a plain-text greeting.

checks.hint: decorated view: @app.route("/") def hello_world(): return "Hello, World!"
run: cd quickstart && flask --app app run --host=0.0.0.0 --port 8080

steps.goal: Start the built-in development server bound to all interfaces on the lab port.

checks.hint: run: cd quickstart && flask --app app run --host=0.0.0.0 --port 8080

steps.goal: Move the response into a Jinja2 template rendered with render_template().

checks.hint: create quickstart/templates/index.html
import render_template and return render_template("index.html")
the served page must come from templates/index.html

steps.goal: Restart the server and confirm the rendered template is what the browser receives.

checks.hint: stop the server (Ctrl+C) and run flask --app app run --host=0.0.0.0 --port 8080 again

steps.goal: Accept a name in the URL and pass it to the template as dynamic context.

checks.hint: add @app.route("/<name>") with def hello(name)

template must render

Hello, {{ name }}!

steps.goal: Verify dynamic routing end to end through a real HTTP request.

checks.hint: browse to http://localhost:8080/Nairobi
any name segment must be reflected in the greeting

steps.goal: Confirm the template engine and web framework are both installed in the runtime.

checks.hint: pip install Flask
pip install Jinja2 (Flask already pulls it in)

steps.goal: Create the templates-lab application that renders a template instead of a string.

checks.hint: define app = Flask(__name__), @app.route('/') def index(): return render_template('index.html')

steps.goal: Author the Jinja2 template that the index view renders.

checks.hint: create templates-lab/templates/index.html
keep the if __name__ == '__main__': app.run(debug=True) guard

steps.goal: Run the app and check the template is served at http://localhost:8080.

checks.contains: Welcome to Flask Jinja2 Templates Lab

steps.goal: Create the devserver-lab application module used for the whole module.

checks.hint: app = Flask(__name__) with @app.route('/') def hello(): return 'Hello, Flask!'

steps.goal: Start the development server through the Flask CLI rather than python app.py.

checks.hint: cd devserver-lab && flask --app app run --host=0.0.0.0 --port 8080 (this step checks YOUR running server, it will not start one for you)

checks.hint: cd devserver-lab && flask --app app run --debug --host=0.0.0.0 --port 8080

steps.goal: Point the CLI at a differently named application file with --app.

checks.hint: copy app.py to myapp.py (a second entry point is fine)
flask --app myapp run --host=0.0.0.0 --port 8080

steps.goal: Diagnose a port conflict with lsof / ss / netstat before choosing a new port.
steps.note: Diagnosis step: there is no file artefact. The commands are shown so you can run them yourself; step 17 proves you recovered by serving on a free port.

steps.goal: Start the server from Python code with the __main__ guard and app.run(debug=True).

checks.hint: add: if __name__ == "__main__":  app.run(debug=True)

steps.goal: Have the Flask package importable for the CLI exercises.

checks.hint: pip install flask

steps.goal: Write the cli-lab application that the CLI will discover.

checks.hint: create cli-lab/app.py with app = Flask(__name__) and a hello view

steps.goal: Serve the app with flask run instead of python app.py.

checks.hint: cd cli-lab && flask --app app run --host=0.0.0.0 --port 8080

steps.goal: Build a standalone click command that prints a greeting.

checks.hint: create cli-lab/commands.py using @click.command() and @click.argument('name')
python commands.py John must print the greeting

steps.goal: Create the flaskr package directory inside the flaskr-app project.

checks.hint: cd flaskr-app && mkdir flaskr

steps.goal: Write the application factory that instantiates and configures the app.

checks.hint: define def create_app(test_config=None): returning a Flask instance
app.config.from_mapping(SECRET_KEY='dev', ...) inside create_app

steps.goal: Load instance/test config, create the instance folder, and add the hello route.

checks.hint: create flaskr/db.py with get_db() and close_db()

call db.init_app(app) inside create_app

steps.goal: Create the auth blueprint module with its URL prefix.

checks.hint: from . import auth  then  app.register_blueprint(auth.bp)
create_app() must register the 'auth' blueprint

steps.goal: Implement the registration view that stores a hashed password.

checks.hint: @bp.route('/register', methods=('GET', 'POST')) def register():

steps.goal: Implement the login view that checks the password hash and opens a session.

checks.hint: @bp.route('/login', methods=('GET','POST')) def login():
GET /auth/login must render a form with a password input

steps.goal: Add the logout view that clears the session.

checks.hint: @bp.route('/logout') must clear the session and redirect to index

checks.hint: def login_required(view) using functools.wraps

checks.name: auth_guard.py

steps.goal: Create the stylesheet file inside the static folder.

checks.hint: touch flaskr/static/style.css

steps.goal: Fill the stylesheet with the layout rules for the application.

checks.hint: style.css needs real declarations for html, body and nav

checks.hint: create flaskr/blog.py importing login_required and get_db

steps.goal: List every post with its author, newest first.

checks.hint: @bp.route('/') def index() querying post JOIN user ordered by created DESC

steps.goal: Let a logged-in user create a post that is written to the database.

steps.goal: Let the author edit their own post.

checks.hint: @bp.route('/<int:id>/update', methods=('GET','POST')) @login_required def update(id):

checks.name: blog_update.py

steps.goal: Let the author delete their own post.

checks.hint: @bp.route('/<int:id>/delete', methods=('POST',)) @login_required def delete(id):

steps.goal: Create the config-lab application that configuration will be attached to.

checks.hint: app = Flask(__name__) with a hello view

steps.goal: Set DEBUG and SECRET_KEY directly on app.config.

checks.hint: app.config['DEBUG'] = True and app.config['SECRET_KEY'] = 'mysecretkey'

steps.goal: Install the blinker package that Flask uses for signals.

checks.hint: pip install flask blinker

steps.goal: Import Flask and blinker's Namespace in the signals application.

checks.hint: from flask import Flask; from blinker import Namespace

steps.goal: Instantiate the Flask application object.

checks.hint: app = Flask(__name__)

checks.hint: my_signals = Namespace()

checks.name: signals_namespace.py
checks.hint: my_signals must be a blinker.Namespace instance

steps.goal: Define a named application signal.

checks.hint: model_saved = my_signals.signal('model-saved')

checks.name: signals_define.py
checks.hint: model_saved must be a blinker signal named 'model-saved'

steps.goal: Subscribe a receiver function to the signal.

checks.hint: def on_model_saved(sender) decorated with @model_saved.connect

checks.name: signals_subscribe.py
checks.hint: the signal must have at least one connected receiver

steps.goal: Emit the signal and confirm the receiver runs.

checks.hint: model_saved.send(app)

checks.name: signals_emit.py
checks.hint: sending the signal must run the receiver and print Model saved!

steps.goal: Run the application that emits the signal during startup.

checks.hint: cd signals-lab && python app.py --port 8080 (or flask --app app run --port 8080); the lab needs YOUR server running for this check

steps.goal: Open the Flask shell and inspect the application and request context interactively.
steps.note: Interactive step: flask shell opens a Python REPL inside an app context, so it leaves no file artefact to grade. Run the commands in the terminal and read what they print, then continue to step 62.

checks.hint: with app.test_request_context('/?page=2'): read request.url and request.args
python shell.py must print the request URL from the pushed context

steps.goal: Fire the before-request and after-request functions from a script.

checks.hint: call app.preprocess_request() and app.process_response(response) inside the context

steps.goal: Expose helper functions to the shell with a shell context processor.

checks.hint: shelltools.py must define initialize_database() and drop_tables()
register app.shell_context_processor(make_shell_context) returning the helpers

pip install coverage

checks.hint: tests/data.sql holds the sample user and post rows
conftest.py must create the app with a temp db path, init it from data.sql, and expose app/client/runner fixtures
pytest must collect without import errors

steps.goal: Test the application factory: configuration and the hello view.

checks.hint: test_config asserts the SECRET_KEY default; test_index checks the hello response
python -m pytest -q tests/test_factory.py must pass

checks.hint: the auth suite needs test_register and test_login_logout_edit (plus the auth helper fixture)

steps.goal: Render user input through Jinja2 autoescaping so a script tag stays inert data.

checks.hint: a / view that renders the name through a template (not render_template_string of raw input)
GET /?name=<script>alert(1)</script> must come back escaped, never as a live tag

steps.goal: Reject a state-changing request that carries no CSRF token, accept one that does.

checks.hint: a GET form view that issues a session token and a POST /delete that verifies it

checks.name: csrf_guard.py
checks.hint: POST /delete without the token must be refused; with the token from the served form it must succeed

steps.goal: Confirm the framework version that parses JSON only through Flask's safe provider.

checks.hint: pip install --upgrade Flask (the lab targets Flask 3.x, whose JSON provider is the mitigation)

steps.goal: Add the response headers that constrain framing, sniffing, policy loading and force HTTPS.

checks.hint: an after_request hook (or Talisman) must set all four headers on every response

steps.goal: Set the session cookie with Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite attributes.

checks.hint: a / view that sets a cookie and configures the session cookie
the Set-Cookie header on / must carry Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax

steps.goal: Understand why HPKP was abandoned and what replaces it.
steps.note: History-and-judgement step. HPKP was removed from browsers (RFC 7469 deprecated) because a bad pin could lock everyone out of a site; the modern equivalent is Certificate Transparency plus short-lived certs and an expect-CT policy. Nothing to build or run, so there is no grader for this step.

steps.goal: Write a view that awaits a coroutine instead of blocking the worker.

checks.hint: async def get_data() under @app.route('/get-data'), awaiting async_db_query()
GET /get-data must return the JSON payload produced by the awaited query

steps.goal: Build a wheel for the flaskr project so it can be installed on a server.

checks.hint: pip install build
cd flaskr-app && python -m build --wheel (the wheel must land in dist/)

steps.goal: Install the built wheel and run the CLI against the installed package.

checks.hint: pip install flaskr-app/dist/flaskr-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl, then python -c "import flaskr; print(flaskr.__file__)" must resolve inside site-packages
from the workspace root (outside the source tree) flask --app flaskr init-db must work

steps.goal: Give the installed application a real secret key in its instance folder.

checks.hint: write SECRET_KEY = '<token from python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex())">' into flaskr-app/instance/config.py

checks.name: instance_secret.py
checks.hint: create_app() must load an instance SECRET_KEY that is not the 'dev' default and is at least 16 characters

steps.goal: Serve the application with the Waitress production server and prove it answers.

cd flaskr-app && waitress-serve --listen=0.0.0.0:8080 --call 'flaskr:create_app' (this check talks to YOUR running server)
